data.why: The repo bundles its own demo CSVs (data/demo/earthquakes.csv, exposure_points.csv, sentinel_catalog.csv) read directly by streamlit_app.py for the default Demo mode, so nothing needs to be copied there; the written files are upload-test fixtures for the 'Upload local file' earthquake mode, the exposure-screening CSV uploader, and the optional InSAR displacement-points uploader, matching the exact columns normalise_events/screen_exposure/summarise_displacement expect, with realistic Kahramanmaras 2026 event data plus deliberate defects (a duplicate event_id, a missing depth, an out-of-range latitude, a missing exposure weight) to exercise the quality-report and screening code paths.

goals: Explore the bundled synthetic earthquake catalog and read off event count, max magnitude, median depth, shallow-event share and a Gutenberg-Richter b-value estimate
Switch to Live USGS mode, pick a lookback window and minimum magnitude, and confirm records are pulled from the official USGS FDSN catalog for Turkiye
Upload a local earthquake CSV with messy aliased columns, duplicates and an invalid coordinate and check the data-quality tab flags them correctly
Run the rolling event-rate anomaly screen and DBSCAN spatial clustering on the catalog and interpret flagged anomalies as statistical, not predictive
Upload an exposure-points CSV and screen it against the largest-magnitude events at an adjustable radius to see nearby-point counts and exposure weight
Browse the Sentinel-1 demo acquisition catalog, inspect same-orbit candidate pairs, and upload a processed InSAR displacement CSV to view summary statistics and a displacement map

review.summary: The tree matches what the README says this dashboard is for, its phases and tasks are at the right level, and all eight screens I opened support their nodes. It needs fixes before filing: one finding contradicts the code (exposure screening is limited to the 50 largest events), t4 and t11 need code-backed explanations, the overview charts have no feature, and f8 should be split.
